quoted_tweet.author: Yarchi
quoted_tweet.text:
Andrej Karpathy built an agent that runs AI research autonomously. The whole setup is just 3 files

It's called autoresearch. You give Claude or Codex a small LLM training setup and walk away.

The loop:

> try one idea in http://train.py
> commit
> train for exactly 5 minutes
> if score improved - keep it. Worse - git reset
> log the result, repeat forever

The instructions literally tell the agent to never stop and never ask "should I keep going?", because the human might be asleep.

You don't touch the Python at all. You only edit program.md, the agent's instructions. Karpathy calls it the code of your research org.

There's even a simplicity rule. A tiny gain that adds 20 lines of hacky code gets thrown out. Same score with less code gets kept.

I think this pattern works way beyond LLMs. Anything with one number to beat, one file to edit and a fixed time per run can grind overnight like this.

92k stars, MIT. Runs on one NVIDIA GPU, local or rented, with community forks for Mac, Windows and AMD.

repo: http://github.com/karpathy/autoresearch
